w: Brick Gothic basilica raised in the 14th century in Olsztyn's Old Town, still listed on Poland's register of historic monuments. Named for James the Great, it now holds co-cathedral status for the Catholic diocese - one of the oldest surviving churches in this corner of Warmia.
s: Gothic co-cathedral anchoring Olsztyn's Old Town
_facts: 14th-century Gothic architecture, on Poland's register of monuments
Located in the Old Town area of Olsztyn
Dedicated to James the Great, functions as co-cathedral

w: A 385-metre guyed mast looming over the Pieczewo district, built in 1969 and nicknamed 'Stefan' after Stefan Kaminski, the man credited with bringing television to Olsztyn. Since the Warsaw radio mast's collapse, it has stood as the second-tallest structure in all of Poland.
_facts: Second-tallest structure in Poland since the Warsaw radio mast's collapse
Nicknamed 'Stefan' after Stefan Kaminski, who brought TV to Olsztyn

w: Also known by its old name, Krzywe, Ukiel is Olsztyn's biggest lake, filling a hollow between the Dajtki, Gutkowo and Likusy districts in the northwest of the city. A municipal beach and a scatter of lakeside pensions and hotels make it the default summer escape for locals.
_facts: Olsztyn's largest lake, informally called Krzywe
Sits between the Dajtki, Gutkowo and Likusy districts
Has a municipal beach plus lakeside pensions and hotels

n: Castle of Warmian Bishops in Olsztyn
w: Brick Gothic castle built in the 14th century for administrators of the Warmian Cathedral Chapter's estates - one of them Nicolaus Copernicus, who lived here from 1516 to 1521. Its largest hall, a refectory under a diamond vault raised around 1520, now anchors the Museum of the Warmian-Masurian Voivodeship.
_facts: 14th-century Brick Gothic castle in central Olsztyn
Nicolaus Copernicus resided here 1516-1521 as chapter administrator
Refectory has a diamond vault built around 1520
Now houses the Museum of the Warmian-Masurian Voivodeship

w: A former Jewish Tahara house - where bodies were ritually washed and prepared before burial - standing in Olsztyn along with its old gatehouse. Bet Tahara buildings like this once stood beside nearly every Jewish cemetery in the region; this one survived and now serves as a center for intercultural dialogue.
s: Former Jewish ritual funeral house, still standing
_facts: Former Jewish Tahara (ritual washing) house, with a surviving gatehouse
Now used as a center for intercultural dialogue
